_comment: What a blacksmith can forge. Engine data, not a campaign's: every realm's smithy works the same. 'cost' is what ONE takes out of the province's own stores — the recipes Lords of the Realm's guides give, iron and timber only, still to be confirmed against the original's table — and the four stats are 0..10 bars. How many a season the forge turns out is the smiths' (GameBalance.SmithsPerWeapon), not the file's.

items.name: Bows
items.blurb: Cheap to make and quick to learn. Thins a charge long before it reaches the line.

items.name: Crossbows
items.blurb: Slow to wind, but a bolt goes through mail where an arrow turns. Anyone can be taught to aim one.

items.name: Swords
items.blurb: Well-balanced swords for disciplined infantry. Reliable in close combat and easy to arm in large numbers.

items.name: Pikes
items.blurb: A hedge of points that horses will not ride into. Little use once a line is broken.

items.name: Cavalry
items.blurb: The costliest thing a province can raise, and the only one that decides a field in a single charge.

items.name: Maces
items.blurb: Crude, heavy, and indifferent to armour. What a smith forges when there is iron but no time.
